content:
The Barr body is an inactivated X chromosome in female mammalian cells, which is highly condensed and transcriptionally inactive.  
Euchromatin is loosely packed and transcriptionally active, so it cannot be the Barr body.  
Heterochromatin is tightly packed and generally inactive, which matches the description of the Barr body.  
A cistron is a gene or coding sequence, not applicable here.  
Pseudogenes are nonfunctional gene copies, unrelated to X inactivation.  

Final answer: (B)
